summary: Sierra Leone admits ECOWAS citizens visa-free and issues nearly everyone else a visa on arrival — USD 25 for African Union nationals, USD 80 for most others and free for a handful of African states — with the official eVisa portal (evisa.sl) as the apply-ahead alternative.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Sierra Leone requires proof of yellow fever vaccination from all arriving travelers. The yellow card is checked by port health officers at Lungi airport and land borders.

source.name: Government of Sierra Leone — official e-Visa portal

travelInsurance.text: Not required for entry, but strongly recommended with medical-evacuation coverage — hospital care is very limited, even in Freetown.

source.name: Government of Sierra Leone — official e-Visa portal

onwardTicket.text: Not formally published as an entry condition, but airlines commonly ask for a return or onward ticket before boarding.

source.name: Government of Sierra Leone — official e-Visa portal

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show means of support for their stay.

source.name: Government of Sierra Leone — official e-Visa portal

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency above USD 10,000 (or equivalent) should be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Sierra Leonean customs before carrying large sums.

notes: Diamond and precious-mineral exports are tightly controlled — buying or carrying uncertified stones is a criminal offense.

payments.text: Cash rules. Cards are accepted only at a few Freetown hotels and restaurants, and ATMs that take foreign cards are unreliable. Bring clean, recent US dollar notes to exchange, and note that prices are sometimes still quoted in pre-2022 "old" leones (a thousand times the new unit).

safety.text: Sierra Leone has been peaceful since 2002 and visitors are generally welcomed warmly. The main risks are petty theft in Freetown, road accidents and occasional political demonstrations. Avoid crowds, and take care on the roads at night.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Sierra Leone Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is the dry season — best for the peninsula beaches, Tiwai Island and up-country roads; May to October brings some of the heaviest rainfall in Africa.

idp.text: Sierra Leone is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Sierra Leone is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Sierra Leone yet.

tips.text: If you plan to get the visa on arrival, bring the fee in exact US dollar cash, or skip the line by applying ahead on the official portal, evisa.sl.
Lungi airport sits across the estuary from Freetown. The sea coach (water taxi) is the standard transfer and meets flights, but plan connections so you're not crossing late at night.
From May to October Sierra Leone gets torrential rain — among the heaviest in Africa. Up-country roads deteriorate fast and some become impassable; build slack into any wet-season itinerary.
Your yellow fever certificate is checked on arrival — every traveler needs one, whatever country you fly in from.
Bring crisp, large-denomination US dollar bills — worn or small notes get poor rates or are refused. Confirm whether quoted prices are in new leones (SLE) or colloquial "old" leones.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Sierra Leone?
faq.answer: ECOWAS citizens enter visa-free. Almost everyone else can get a visa on arrival at Lungi airport and other entry points — USD 25 for African Union passport holders, USD 80 for most other nationalities, free for citizens of a few African states, or apply in advance through the official eVisa portal, evisa.sl.

faq.question: How much is the Sierra Leone visa on arrival?
faq.answer: USD 80 for most nationalities, reduced to USD 25 for citizens of non-ECOWAS African Union countries, and issued free to nationals of Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi and Mauritius. Pay in cash. Bring exact US dollars.

faq.question: Does Sierra Leone have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes — the official Government of Sierra Leone portal at evisa.sl issues e-visas ahead of travel, with fees tiered by nationality. It covers the same short tourist and business stays as the visa on arrival and avoids queuing at Lungi.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Sierra Leone?
faq.answer: Yes. All arriving travelers must show a yellow fever vaccination certificate, regardless of where they fly in from.

faq.question: Is Sierra Leone safe to visit?
faq.answer: Generally yes. The country has been at peace since 2002 and the beach and wildlife circuit is relaxed and friendly. Use normal city precautions in Freetown, avoid demonstrations, and treat night-time road travel with respect.
